description: The conference Wi-Fi keeps cutting out mid-session in Hall B. I spend most keynotes reconnecting my laptop instead of watching slides.
Guest network bandwidth is dreadful in the big rooms. Video calls stall and the slide decks never finish preloading.
Wi-Fi in Hall B dies every couple of minutes. Stuck spinning on reconnect screens through the whole afternoon track.
Feels like the venue throttled the wireless — a two-meg PDF takes forever to load that I gave up and fired up my phone as a hotspot.
The free venue wireless is basically decorative. Pages hang, my demo repository refuses to sync, and the demo will fail without network.
Signal is fine but throughput is pitiful on the mezzanine. Slack cannot even send a one-line message while a keynote is running.
Every break, half the room is holding their phones up looking for usable wifi. Once a live demo starts, the connection saturates and drops everyone.
Streaming the morning talk from the overflow room was hopeless — video buffers ten seconds, plays two, dies again. Same story yesterday.
Registration portal rejects my Gmail address every time on the captive portal. Ended up tethering off my phone for two mornings.
The wifi sign-in page just spins and never completes the auth step, tried on two different laptops with the day pass code.
Captive portal denies anyone not using Safari. Our delegation of six could not pass the login screen on Android all morning.
Mic kept dropping out and questions shouted from the floor were impossible to make out. Half the panel discussion was guesswork.
Room audio is far too quiet in the back — people on the last rows only hear a mumble. Could the AV team boost the PA?
The handheld mic screeched feedback twice during the talk and then cut completely for a few awkward minutes.
Q&A ambushed the left half of the audience: the runner mic never crossed the aisle, so our questions never made it on the recording.
A microphone popped and crackled the entire slot until panelists grabbed a backup one; the audience hear a nasty buzz whenever it moved.
Floor maps stop at level 2 — zero signage for the west breakout rooms, so every newcomer circles before finding them.
Took me fifteen minutes to locate Room 2.20. The names printed on the doors do not match the app listings at all.
Direction signs use poetic names like 'Sky Gallery' and 'Terrace' instead of room numbers. First-timers are lost anywhere outside the expo floor.
No directional signs where the elevator meets the expo hall — walked a full loop past fifty booths before spotting the track rooms.
A group of us from the lightning talk wandered between buildings hunting for the right room; literally nothing is labeled out there.
Vegan sandwiches sold out by 12:15 sharp. What remained under the warmers was bread and a regrettable amount of dairy.
Buffets at lunch have essentially no plant-based mains. Every apparent veggie dish turned out to be dressed with cheese or egg.
Vegetarian counter had exactly two offerings today and both contained dairy. My colleague ate french fries both afternoons.
For a conference of this size, not offering a proper vegan lunch at the ticket price we paid is genuinely poor form.
The espresso kiosk was bone dry before the first break even ended. Forty people stood in a line that led nowhere.
Morning coffee urns on level 3 emptied by 9:40 both days. Latecomers leave the break with nothing.
Snack tables got cleared half an hour before the afternoon break was actually over. Whoever planned quantities undershot badly.
Whole break queue drifted to the coffee place in the shopping arcade next door because the venue had nothing left to pour.
Reserved wheelchair spaces in Hall A were roped off for camera rigs on day one. A visitor using a wheelchair had to watch from the aisle.
Step-free entry to the main hall only works from the south doors — nothing signposts the ramp at the north entrance either.
The accessible seating markers up front get occupied by early campers who hold the spots all morning. Please enforce them.
The nursing room on level 2 stayed locked all morning while a staffer kept saying 'temporarily'. One look inside would have fixed this.
Lactation room has no power socket working inside, so pumping with an electric pump is off the table, and the key desk closes at noon.
Not a single free chair in the corridor between the halls at any point between sessions. Hundreds of us sit on the floor.
Overflow chairs promised for the infra deep-dive never arrived — dozens of folks ended up leaning on walls for ninety minutes.
Every lounge couch is claimed by 10am and never released. Nowhere to sit and work on a laptop all day.
Breakout 3.1 felt like a walk-in fridge the whole afternoon; the HVAC there seems stuck on max. Gloves stayed on during the whole deep dive.
The big hall slowly cooks by the 3pm slot — air conditioning clearly cannot keep pace with a full room after lunch.
Wildly inconsistent: one breakout room blasts arctic air while the corridor next door is a sauna. Someone will get sick.
Registration queue snaked out of the lobby doorway at 8am and I spent twenty-five minutes outside in the wind just to collect a badge.
The latecomer wave jammed the badge pickup desks around 1pm with nobody directing traffic or opening extra terminals.
Badge printer refused to encode mine, and staff sent me back and forth between two help desks before anyone could reprint it.
Room clash again: the cloud workshop and a security panel were both booked into 3.40 simultaneously, and the host apologized twice for the confusion.
Same-slot collision once more — half the workshop audience stood outside a room where a different session was running late.
The Monday 10:30 slot lists two different tracks in 2.06; both hosts showed up and renegotiated outside the door on the spot.
Left my rain shell at the coat check during the keynote — does the desk coordinate with lost and found, or is that a separate office?
Airport shuttle runs vanished from the posted timetable after 6pm, leaving evening departures guessing which stop to camp at.
Closing keynote recording has shown 'processing' in the portal for two days now. Several teams referenced it for their internal follow-up.
Exhibitors started blasting demo audio into the hallway right where the lightning talk stage sits. The speaker had to stop and wait for the ad jingle to finish.
The shirt stand shut its line while roughly a hundred people were still queuing for it. No announcement, no restock, nothing.
The elevator to the mezzanine is out of service and there is no alternative ramp nearby. Pushing a stroller up with a toddler is a bad time.
Anyone know a quiet café with acceptable cappuccino somewhere near the venue? Asking for Thursday morning.
Selling one spare day pass at face value for tomorrow, message me directly if you want it.
We need one or two more players for tonight's board-game meetup in the hotel bar, all welcome.
First time in this city — any favorite running routes along the river front before sessions start?
Registration to first workshop took under ten minutes this year. Kudos to the volunteer crew, everything felt organized.
Everything from breakfast to the closing panel has been great so far — clean rooms, friendly staff, even the audio was crisp.
Zero complaints from our team: fast network, solid lunch spread, sessions kicked off precisely on time all morning.
Lovely conference so far. The demo zone staff were patient and helpful, and the quiet areas are a wonderful touch.
